Subject: Composite discount proposal + reseller uplift — DataWorks Azure private offer

Hi Anna,

Great to meet yesterday — thanks for the time. As promised, attaching a concise worksheet that lays out a two-part structure we think will work for DataWorks on Azure Marketplace: a list-price discount band (applies to the private offer) + an explicit reseller uplift (pass-through) so your partners keep a healthy margin. The goal is to give procurement predictable net pricing while preserving partner economics.

Key highlights in the attachment:
- Base private-offer discount: 18% off MSRP list price (applies to all metered SKU lines).
- Volume band incentives: additional 3% at $500k, 5% at $1M ARR (12-month lookback).
- Reseller uplift: 7% of gross invoice value paid to named partners (no double-dipping against volume bands).
- List-price floor: 40% of published price (to prevent downstream over-discounting).

Ask: can you confirm if procurement needs the list-price floor spelled out on the PO itself, or if a separate clause (we can provide template language) is sufficient? Also curious whether one named reseller or an open list is preferred for the uplift.

I copied Camila (Ops) to validate invoicing flow and Laura (Deals) for contract language. If this looks reasonable, we can generate the private-offer draft and a short SOW for signature.

Thanks —
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: DW-DataWorks-Azure-Offer-worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet); Redwood-DPA.pdf (redwood standard DPA)

Sergio,

Thanks — worksheet looks clear. A couple quick questions from procurement and finance:

1) List-price floor: Procurement prefers an explicit floor on the PO so our internal systems (for compliance) capture it. Can you add the sentence: "List-price floor shall be 40% of published list price and reflected on the private offer invoice" to the draft?
2) Reseller uplift: We typically name 2-3 approved resellers on the PO. Is the 7% uplift payable only to named resellers, or would Redwood support an "approved partner list" maintained by DataWorks?
3) Billing cadence: if we take the 12-month commitment approach, billing will be monthly metered. We need to ensure uplift accounting is computed monthly (not at true-up).

Also can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to include a one-time implementation credit (we discussed $25k) that can be drawn down over the first 90 days? That would help get the pilot greenlit.

Anna Cho
Head of Cloud Procurement | DataWorks Inc.

Sergio — quick ops check: we can provide monthly uplift calculation as a discrete line on the invoice so partners can reconcile. That requires:
- Partner-fee mapping table (SKU -> uplift %) included in the PO or an attached schedule (we should attach the "partner-fee-schedule.csv").
- Named-reseller flow: when a named reseller is present on the PO, we route uplift payments to the named partner ID. If open list chosen, we'd require partner enrollment ahead of first invoice to bind payout.

On the list-price floor visibility: ops is neutral as long as the floor is administrative only. The caveat is accounting teams sometimes flag "floor" language as indicative of a controlled-price arrangement. Suggest Laura draft the minimal clause to keep procurement happy while limiting accounting exposure.

I will prepare a ready-to-send private-offer draft and a short internal ops checklist for partner payout (will attach as partner-uplift-checklist.pdf).

Hi Anna,

Thanks for the clear feedback. We can add the exact sentence you requested to the private offer draft. To limit downstream accounting questions we'll use this language (suggested clause):

"List-price floor: For administrative and invoice-routing purposes the list-price floor is set at 40% of Redwood's published list price. This administrative floor is not intended to modify Redwood's published price schedule or to create a separate pricing commitment outside the private offer."

Regarding reseller uplift: Redwood will pay the 7% uplift to named resellers listed on the private offer for the first 90 days. After 90 days DataWorks may provide an approved-partner list to extend eligibility; Redwood requires partner enrollment form to be completed before the first uplift payment. We will reflect the uplift as a discrete line item on monthly invoices.

Implementation credit: we will apply a one-time $25,000 non-recurring implementation credit to your first invoice; this will be listed as "Implementation credit (pilot)".

If that language works for procurement, Sergio will circulate a redline private-offer and I can attach the DPA and the partner-uplift-checklist for your legal/ops teams.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
